record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Tagged-leaf height in original interval model
record.original_question: In the original interval-splitting version of the critical beta-splitting model, where one follows a specified leaf i(n) rather than a uniformly random leaf, determine the distribution of the height of that leaf in both DTCS(n), the discrete-time tree built by recursive interval splitting, and CTCS(n), its continuous-time version in which a clade of size m splits after an Exponential(h_{m-1}) time.

evidence.quote: Continue until reaching intervals of size 1, which are the leaves. That is a discrete time construction, which we call3 DTCS(n).
Open Problem 2 In the original interval-splitting model, analyze the distribution of the height of the leaf i(n) in DTCS(n) and CTCS(n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $n\ge 2$ and consider the following interval-splitting construction of a random binary tree with $n$ leaves labelled $1,2,\dots,n$.

Discrete-time model DTCS(n). Start with the interval $[0,n]$, regarded as the root, containing the $n$ unit subintervals $[i-1,i]$, $i=1,\dots,n$, called "leaf-points." Recursively, any interval $[a,b]$ of integer length $m=b-a\ge 2$ that has not yet been split is split into two subintervals $[a,a+J]$ and $[a+J,b]$, where the split position $J\in\{1,2,\dots,m-1\}$ is chosen with the critical beta-splitting probabilities
$$q(m,j)=\frac{1}{h_{m-1}}\Big(\frac{1}{j}+\frac{1}{m-j}\Big)\cdot\frac{1}{2},\qquad j=1,\dots,m-1,$$
where $h_{k}=\sum_{r=1}^{k}1/r$ is the $k$-th harmonic number. (Equivalently, $q(m,j)=\frac{1}{h_{m-1}}\cdot\frac{1}{j(m-j)}\cdot\frac{m}{2}$ after symmetrisation.) Splits at distinct intervals are independent. The recursion stops when every remaining interval has length $1$; these unit intervals are the leaves and inherit the labels $1,\dots,n$ from their positions. The resulting rooted binary tree is DTCS(n), and the height of a leaf is the number of edges on the path from the root to that leaf.

Continuous-time model CTCS(n). The same recursive splitting is performed, but each unsplit interval of integer length $m\ge 2$ waits an independent $\mathrm{Exponential}(h_{m-1})$ time before splitting (with split position again distributed as $q(m,\cdot)$). The height of a leaf in CTCS(n) is the total continuous time elapsed from the root split down to that leaf.

For each $n\ge 2$, let $i(n)\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ be a prescribed (deterministic) leaf label; for instance $i(n)=1$, or more generally any sequence with $i(n)/n\to\alpha\in[0,1]$. Determine the distribution of the height of leaf $i(n)$ in DTCS(n) and the distribution of the height of leaf $i(n)$ in CTCS(n), and describe their asymptotic behaviour as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent follow-up work on the critical beta-splitting model (including Mellin-analytic studies and central limit theorems for leaf height) explicitly restricts attention to a uniformly random leaf. The Mellin-analysis paper states that its results "do not use the leaf-labels {1,…,n} in the interval-splitting construction" and concern only a uniform random leaf. No located source resolves the distribution of the height of a specified labelled leaf $i(n)$ in DTCS(n) or CTCS(n), so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree IV: Mellin analysis of Leaf Height
status_evidence.snippet: Our results do not use the leaf-labels {1,2,…,n} in the interval-splitting construction. Instead they involve a uniform random leaf.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent analysis treats only uniformly random leaves, not a specified leaf i(n).

status_evidence.title: Some central limit theorems for critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: Ln and Dn denote the heights of a leaf chosen uniformly at random in the discrete and continuous versions of a critical beta-splitting tree.
status_evidence.claim: CLT-type results for leaf heights in DTCS(n) and CTCS(n) only address uniformly random leaves.
